narration.text: Imagine hiding in a winepress, threshing wheat in secret, because every harvest ends up stolen. That is where we first meet Gideon.

image.prompt: A young man threshing wheat in secret inside a stone winepress, golden-hour light through a gap in the wall, painterly ancient Near East, no text, no lettering, no watermark

scenes.notes: Hook within 10 seconds. Open loop: why would 300 be enough?

narration.text: For seven years, Midian had overrun the land. Israel lived in caves and mountain strongholds, and many were afraid.

image.prompt: A wide valley at dusk with distant raiders' tents, families sheltering in mountain caves, painterly ancient Near East, no text, no lettering, no watermark

narration.text: Into that fear, a messenger appears and calls Gideon a mighty warrior. Gideon does not feel like one. He asks questions, and he asks for signs.

image.prompt: A hesitant young man beneath an old tree meeting a radiant figure in soft light, painterly ancient Near East, no text, no lettering, no watermark

scenes.notes: Use the local WEB text for any verse shown on screen; none is quoted in this sample.

narration.text: Many see the fleece as an act of honest doubt, and others as a model for prayer. Either way, the story stays patient with him.

image.prompt: A wool fleece on a threshing floor, wet with morning dew in soft dawn light, painterly ancient Near East, no text, no lettering, no watermark

scenes.notes: Interpretation is hedged ('many see'); flag for Auditor as an interpretive claim.

narration.text: Then comes the surprise. The army is too large. Thousands go home, until only three hundred remain.

image.prompt: A vast encampment thinning to a small band of men standing near a spring at dusk, painterly ancient Near East, no text, no lettering, no watermark

scenes.notes: Pays off the open loop from scene 1.

narration.text: In the night, trumpets sound and jars break, and torches blaze on the hillside. The camp of Midian is thrown into confusion. The story closes with a quiet question: where do we place our trust?
